correctness.rationale: Sorting a supporting covector with three distinct levels gives an ordered partition; strict ordering of the generator ensures dimension n−3 and prevents collapsing faces. The ridge lies in the two nested-subset facets. Sum-zero projections of their normals have product ac/n and squared norms a(b+c)/n and c(a+b)/n, so the interior angle is the supplement of their acute separation. Counting ordered partitions gives the stated multinomial measure conditioned on nonempty blocks. The cyclic exterior cotangents have pairwise products a/n,b/n,c/n; their sum of angles is π, proving the exact mean by cyclic invariance. Independently put q=B/n, t=q−1/3 and d=(A−C)/(2n). The angle is π/2+atan(sqrt(((1−q)²/4−d²)/q)), hence its d=0 part is π−2 atan(sqrt(q)) and its d² coefficient is −4 sqrt(q)/[(1−q)(1+q)²]. Expanding gives L=−3 sqrt(3)t/4, Q=sqrt(3)(27t²/32−9d²/8), C=−sqrt(3)(81t³/64+27td²/16). The one-draw centered coordinates (T,D)=(2/3,0),(−1/3,1/2),(−1/3,−1/2) are equiprobable. Their variances are 2/9 and 1/6, covariance zero, and third moments E[T³]=2/27 and E[TD²]=−1/18. The linear term gives the CLT and 3/(8n); the cubic contribution 2LQ has expectation −9/(16n²). Pairings of draws give E[Q²+2LC]=99/(64n²)+O(n⁻³) (exactly 99(2n−1)/(128n³) including the one-draw terms). Degree-five centered moments and absolute sixth moments are O(n⁻³); outside a fixed balanced neighborhood the bounded angle contributes exponentially little, as does conditioning on nonempty blocks. Thus the net coefficient is 63/64. The sole size triple at n=3 gives zero variance; for n≥4 cyclic placements of n−2 in (n−2,1,1) yield different angles.
residual_risks: The checker enumerates small dimensions and verifies symbolic moments; it does not explicitly compare finite variances to the asymptotic curve as the prose also suggests. The proof does not depend on that comparison.

value.rationale: Count-sampled dihedral concentration is a natural statistic on this classical fan, distinct from the traditional angle sum. The exact second-order term quantifies convergence and can distinguish fans that share the same leading normal law. It is evaluated by geometric and fourth-order sampling calculations, not supplied by the known aggregate mean or a parameter substitution.
residual_risks: Value is for the uniform-ridge law and quantified variance, not a new normal-fan or angle-sum theorem.
